s0101.literal: Soon he was given the credential staff, made area commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, Pacify-the-East General, and Administrator of Wuxing.
s0101.idiomatic: Soon he received the credential staff and was made area commander of Wuxing military affairs, Pacify-the-East general, and administrator of Wuxing.

s0102.literal: In year 4 he entered the capital as Palace Attendant and Forward Aide General; he was moved to Pacify-the-Front General and Central Army Inspector.
s0102.idiomatic: In year 4 he entered the capital as palace attendant and forward aide general, then became pacify-the-front general and central army inspector.

s0103.literal: In year 7 he went out with the credential staff as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of all military affairs in the four provinces South Xu, South Yu, North Xu, and North Yan, Pacify-the-North General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
s0103.idiomatic: In year 7 he went out bearing the credential staff as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, area commander of South Xu, South Yu, North Xu, and North Yan, pacify-the-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

s0104.literal: Bogu by nature loved wine and did not like to hoard; the salary he received was spent without measure; after deep drunkenness he often begged from others; among all the princes he was poorest, and Emperor Gaozong often pitied him and gave him special rewards.
s0104.idiomatic: Bogu loved wine and would not save; his salary vanished without plan, and when drunk he often begged from others. Among the princes he was the poorest, and Emperor Gaozong often pitied him and gave special gifts.

s0105.literal: Bogu's natural disposition was frivolous; he liked to wield the whip; in the province he paid no heed to government affairs; by day he went out hunting, sometimes riding a sleeping litter into the grass, then calling commoners to follow his excursions—often for ten days at a stretch; the deer and boar he caught he mostly had brought in alive; Emperor Gaozong knew of this fairly well and several times sent envoys to rebuke him.
s0105.idiomatic: Bogu was frivolous by nature and fond of the whip. In his province he ignored government, hunted by day, sometimes rode a sleeping litter into the meadows, and called commoners to join him for outings that could last ten days. The deer and boar he took he mostly had brought in alive. Emperor Gaozong knew of it and sent envoys to rebuke him more than once.

s0106.literal: In year 10 he came to court and again became Palace Attendant and Pacify-the-Right General; soon he was made Protector of the Army General.
s0106.idiomatic: In year 10 he came to court and again became palace attendant and pacify-the-right general; soon he was made protector of the army general.

s0107.literal: That year he was made libationer of the National University and concurrently led the Left Valiant Cavalry; Palace Attendant and Pacify-the-Right remained as before.
s0107.idiomatic: That year he was made libationer of the National University and concurrently led the left valiant cavalry; palace attendant and pacify-the-right remained unchanged.

s0108.literal: Bogu was fairly versed in arcane principle, yet in his studies he mastered nothing; when it came to posing lines and challenging with questions, he often had striking ideas.
s0108.idiomatic: Bogu knew something of arcane learning yet mastered no art; when he posed lines and pressed others in debate, he often showed a striking turn of mind.

s0109.literal: In governing he was harsh and exacting; in the National University there were idle wanderers who did not pursue their studies—he heavily flogged them with the cudgel; the students feared him, and thereby learning advanced considerably.
s0109.idiomatic: As an administrator he was harsh. Students in the National University who idled instead of studying he beat heavily with the cudgel; they feared him, and study thereafter advanced sharply.

s0110.literal: In year 12 he concurrently held Director of the Imperial Clan.
s0110.idiomatic: In year 12 he also held director of the imperial clan.

s0111.literal: In year 13 he was made credential-bearing, area commander of all military affairs in the four provinces Yang, South Xu, East Yang, and South Yu, and Inspector of Yangzhou; Palace Attendant and general remained as before.
s0111.idiomatic: In year 13 he was made credential-bearing area commander of Yang, South Xu, East Yang, and South Yu and inspector of Yangzhou; palace attendant and general remained as before.

s0112.literal: When the Last Ruler was first in the Eastern Palace, he and Bogu were very intimate; Bogu was also skilled at banter and raillery; whenever Emperor Gaozong held a feast, he often had him brought in.
s0112.idiomatic: When the Last Ruler was still crown prince in the Eastern Palace, he and Bogu were very close. Bogu was also skilled at banter, and Emperor Gaozong often summoned him to feasts.

s0113.literal: Shuling was in Jiangzhou and inwardly resented Bogu's favor; he secretly sought flaws and intended to strike him down by law.
s0113.idiomatic: Shuling was in Jiangzhou and resented Bogu's favor; he secretly looked for faults and meant to bring him down by law.

s0114.literal: When Shuling entered court, Bogu feared punishment and fawned to learn his intent; thereupon together they slandered court worthies, reviling in turn civil and military men—even elders of years and high rank they confronted to their faces, fearing nothing.
s0114.idiomatic: When Shuling came to court, Bogu feared punishment and fawned on him to learn his mind; together they slandered court worthies and abused civil and military men in turn—even elders of years and high rank they confronted to the face without fear.

s0115.literal: Bogu by nature loved shooting pheasants; Shuling also loved opening and rifling tombs; when they went out into the wilds they always went together; their feelings therefore greatly harmonized, and they plotted rebellion.
s0115.idiomatic: Bogu loved shooting pheasants and Shuling loved opening tombs; abroad in the wilds they always went together, their feelings matched, and they plotted treason.

s0116.literal: Bogu attended within the forbidden quarters; whenever there was a secret word, he always reported it to Shuling.
s0116.idiomatic: Bogu attended within the palace; whenever there was a secret word he reported it to Shuling.

s0117.literal: When Shuling fled to the Eastern Palace, he sent a messenger to tell Bogu; Bogu rode alone at full speed to join him and helped Shuling direct operations.
s0117.idiomatic: When Shuling fled to the Eastern Palace he sent word to Bogu; Bogu rode alone at full speed to join him and helped direct the fighting.

s0118.literal: Knowing affairs would not succeed, he wished to flee; it happened that the four gates were already shut and he could not get out, so together they made for Baimang Road.
s0118.idiomatic: Seeing the cause was lost, he meant to flee; the four gates were already shut and he could not leave, so together they made for Baimang Road.

s0121.literal: [Rong] arrived; he was killed by mutinous troops; his corpse lay at the gate of the Dongchang hostel; he was twenty-eight.
s0121.idiomatic: [Rong] arrived; mutinous troops killed him; his body lay at the gate of the Dongchang hostel; he was twenty-eight.

s0122.literal: An edict said: "Bogu shared in this rebellion and perished on the road.
s0122.idiomatic: An edict said, "Bogu shared in this rebellion and perished on the road.

s0123.literal: Now, following outside opinion, our mind still cannot bear it; he may specially be allowed burial with commoner rites.
s0123.idiomatic: Following outside opinion, our mind still cannot bear it; he may be buried with commoner rites as a special grace.

s0124.literal: " Another edict said: "Bogu followed the great rebel and cut himself off from Heaven; to leave no descendants is the constant statute.
s0124.idiomatic: " Another edict said, "Bogu followed the great rebel and cut himself off from Heaven; to leave no descendants is the constant statute.

s0125.literal: Yet children know nothing and also share the reed-and-rush tie; to place them among field folk is truly from compassion; and Wang, who bore Bogu, Editorial footnote marker 4. may both be specially pardoned as commoners.
s0125.idiomatic: Yet the children know nothing and share the family tie; to set them among common folk is true compassion; and Wang, who bore Bogu, [4] may both be specially pardoned as commoners.

s0127.literal: The historiographer says: Confucius said, "Wealth and honor are what men desire; if not obtained by the proper way, one does not dwell in them."
s0127.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Confucius said, "Wealth and honor are what men desire; if not obtained by the proper way, one does not dwell in them."

s0128.literal: From emperors and kings down to the common multitude, none lacks distinction between principal wife and concubine, or order between elder and younger.
s0128.idiomatic: From emperors and kings down to the common multitude, none lacks distinction between principal wife and concubine or order between elder and younger.

s0129.literal: Shuling was dangerous, restless, and driven to outstrip others; he then carried out rebellion; sundering his body by the cart-wheel did not reach his crime; defiling pools at his dwelling did not suffice to show his fault—alas!
s0129.idiomatic: Shuling was dangerous, restless, and driven to outstrip others, then carried out rebellion. Sundering his body by the cart-wheel did not reach his crime; defiling pools at his dwelling did not suffice to show his fault—alas!

s0133.literal: [Rong] Chen Zhishen intercepted and stabbed Shuling—emended according to the Southern History; the same below.
s0133.idiomatic: On "[Rong] Chen Zhishen intercepted and stabbed Shuling": emended per the Southern History; the same below.

s0134.literal: Note: the Comprehensive Mirror also reads "Ma Rong"; Hu's note says: "On campaign, men chosen for ease in the saddle and stout of frame ride horses at the fore to enhance the army's bearing—they are called Ma Rong."
s0134.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror also reads Ma Rong; Hu's note says that on campaign men chosen for ease in the saddle and stout frame ride ahead to enhance the army's bearing and are called Ma Rong.

s0135.literal: At that time the followers were destroyed "followers" in the Southern Supervisory edition reads "released"; the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Palace editions read "exterminated."
s0135.idiomatic: On "at that time the followers were destroyed": followers in the Southern Supervisory edition reads released; the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Palace editions read exterminated.

s0136.literal: The Ji edition also reads "exterminated," with a small note below that one reading is "released."
s0136.idiomatic: The Ji edition also reads exterminated, with a small note that one reading is released.

s0137.literal: Wang Feiqin made General Who Subdues the Waves
s0137.idiomatic: On "Wang Feiqin made General Who Subdues the Waves"

s0139.literal: "Wang Feiqin made General Who Subdues the Waves"—in some texts it reads "Staff Rear General"; doubtful.
s0139.idiomatic: "Wang Feiqin made General Who Subdues the Waves"—some texts read Staff Rear General; doubtful.

s0140.literal: And Wang, who bore Bogu Note

s0142.literal: The preface says "Pan Ronghua bore the Prince of Xin'an, Bogu"—this differs from the present text.
s0142.idiomatic: The preface says Pan Ronghua bore Prince of Xin'an Bogu—this differs from the present text.
